title: The open box

item.name: The ballot box
item.line: A biscuit tin with a slot cut in the lid and the committee's wax seal across it. It holds the street's votes on whether the 19th name stays on the Long Spoon.

brief: Last night Lantern Row voted on the name burned back onto the Long Spoon. The box was sealed at 9 pm, in front of the committee.
At 8 this morning the seal is broken and the lid sits loose. The count is at noon.
The secretary is sure somebody has been at the votes. 2 people had reason to be in the room after it was locked.
Before anybody is accused: was anything taken at all?

suspects.name: Ines
suspects.line: Kept the door for the vote and locked the room after it.
suspects.says: I locked up at 9 and went straight home.

suspects.name: Otto
suspects.line: Rehearses in the hall. His choir sang at a wedding that evening.
suspects.says: I was at the wedding until late. Ask anybody who danced.

steps.thing: The roll of voters and the box itself. Everybody who voted signed the roll, and every card in the box can be counted without being read.
steps.fact: 41 names are on the roll and 41 cards are in the box. Whatever happened to the seal, no vote is missing.
steps.lead: Nothing is gone. So why open it? The secretary wrote the tally down at the close and blotted it. Her blotter is still on the desk.

steps.thing: The blotter. The tally sheet went into the safe, but the blotter kept its wet ink, back to front.

steps.fact: At the close, at 9 pm, the box held 38 cards. By morning it held 41. Nothing was taken out. 3 were put in.
steps.lead: It was opened after 9, and the room was locked. Ines had key 4 and says she went straight home. The bus keeps a roll of every fare.

steps.thing: The ticket roll from last night's buses, and the key book from the hall. Each is kept by somebody with no stake in the vote.
steps.fact: Ines handed key 4 in at 9.05 pm and paid her fare on the 9.10. She came back on the 9.50 for her umbrella, which is why she said nothing. The cloakroom is at the door, 2 floors below.
steps.lead: Key 4 was on its hook all night. But the caretaker's board has a label for every key in the building, and 1 more opens that room.

steps.thing: The label strip under the hooks, punched from a label maker in 1 row with no spaces.
steps.fact: Key 9 opens the music cupboard, and the music cupboard is inside the committee room. That key lets its holder into the room at any hour. The choir keeps it.
steps.lead: Somebody with key 9 was in the room after 9. The choir's notice for last night is still pinned by the piano, and it reads oddly.

steps.thing: A rehearsal notice that is really a promise passed in plain sight, to 3 singers who could not stay for the vote.
steps.text: Bravo tenors. Please all bring both reeds and folders. Lola tends the door. Wedding at 7, back by 9.
steps.fact: 3 singers signed the roll at 4 pm and left their votes sealed with their leader, because they sang at a wedding at 7. The rules allow a sealed vote handed over before the close, if it goes in the box.
steps.lead: Nothing taken, 3 cards added, a second key, and a promise. 3 accounts of last night are going round the street. Only 1 can be true.

steps.thing: 3 accounts of the same night, as the street is telling it. Each piece of evidence already on the board strikes 1 of them out.

accounts.text: Somebody opened the box to take votes out and change the result.
Ines came back for more than her umbrella, and opened the box with key 4.
The wedding ran late. 3 votes that had been promised a place arrived after the seal, and were put in anyway.

steps.fact: Chance: after the close at 9 pm. Means: key 9, to the cupboard in the room. Motive: 3 votes left in his keeping.

ending.found: Nothing was taken. 3 votes were put in after the seal, by the man who had promised to carry them. He broke the wax with a thumb and pressed it back, badly.
ending.confession: They sang so the street could have its wedding and its vote. I was not going to lose theirs to a blob of wax. I should have knocked on a door and said so.
ending.after: The committee counts all 41 at noon, and argues about the 3 until 1. Under the last card in the tin is one that is not a vote: a plain card with an open eye.
